summary: Six applied questions, each built on a short business scenario and split into 2 to 4 small parts. Most parts are calculations (mean, median, mode, range and standard deviation, total probability and Bayes, expected value and variance, normal probabilities) followed by a one or two line interpretation or recommendation. One question is on research design: classifying variables, choosing a sampling method and writing a survey item. A formula list and a standard normal table come with the paper; a scientific calculator is allowed.
paper_format: MST Fall 2026 (3 Sep 2026): 6 questions, all compulsory, in sequence. Q1 5 (3 + 2), Q2 5 (3 + 2), Q3 5 (2 + 2 + 1), Q4 6 (2 + 2 + 2), Q5 6 (2 + 2 + 2), Q6 8 (2 + 1 + 3 + 2). Write down assumptions, steps and the formula used.
question_verbs: Explain in one or two sentences
marks_structure: 1 to 3-mark calculation: formula, substitution, answer with units
2-mark interpretation: use your calculated numbers to back a recommendation or name a risk
3-mark reverse normal problem: find the z for a given area, then convert back to x
repeated_topics: Mean, median and mode with an outlier, and which measure to use
Range and sample standard deviation to compare consistency
Types of variables, scales of measurement, stratified sampling
Expected value, expected value of a linear function, variance of a discrete random variable
Normal distribution: between, more than, a percentile target, expected count
sources: Photos of the printed MST paper, OP5302, Fall 2026 (3 Sep 2026), with formula list and standard normal table
